_purpose: A Resonance Commune community on Nimbus struggles to survive when their sanctuary is threatened by multiple factions. Freeborn living outside the system, building something together, facing the choice between fighting, fleeing, or finding a way to become too valuable to destroy.
scenario_hint: Storm Garden is a Resonance Commune settlement built into an abandoned ley-relay station on Nimbus's outer cloud-layer. For fifteen years, they've lived outside the system - no Soulcredit, no pod-registration, just community, shared ritual, and the storms. Now multiple threats are converging: ACG wants to reclaim the station's ley-infrastructure for a new trade route. House of Vox has discovered they're harboring former broadcast-temple workers who know too much. And a Tempest cell wants to use the station's void-proximity for research - whether the commune agrees or not. The commune leaders have to navigate these threats while protecting their people. Combat should be last resort - they don't have the resources for war. Survival means negotiation, misdirection, making themselves valuable, or finding allies. This is about community survival, not individual heroics.

scenario.location: Nimbus - Storm Garden Commune (Abandoned Ley-Relay Station)
scenario.situation: Storm Garden hangs in the perpetual twilight between Nimbus's cloud layers, anchored to an old ley-relay station that the Nexus abandoned fifty years ago. Two hundred people live here now - Freeborn, former pod-citizens who walked away, children born in the storms. No Soulcredit. No Codex registration. Just community. This morning, three ships appeared at the edge of scanner range: ACG survey vessel, House of Vox information-retrieval team, and an unmarked craft your contacts say is Tempest. They all want something. None of them will simply leave. And Storm Garden has maybe forty people who can fight, limited supplies, and nowhere else to go. The council has called an emergency meeting. You are the commune's problem-solvers - the ones who deal with the outside world. Find a way to make sure Storm Garden still exists by the time the storms take those ships away.

starting_clocks.name: ACG Patience
starting_clocks.description: How long before ACG attempts forcible acquisition of the station
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: demands escalate, ultimatums issued, force authorized
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: negotiations proceed, alternative sites offered, time bought

starting_clocks.name: Vox Information Hunt
starting_clocks.description: How close Vox is to finding their targets in the commune
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: scanning intensifies, informants questioned, raid planned
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: false trails laid, targets hidden, Vox distracted

starting_clocks.name: Tempest Pressure
starting_clocks.description: How insistent Tempest is about using the station for research
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: offers become threats, research begins without consent
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: alternative arrangements, Tempest convinced to look elsewhere

starting_clocks.name: Community Cohesion
starting_clocks.description: How unified the commune remains under pressure
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: factions form, arguments, some want to surrender/flee
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: leadership trusted, community rallies, unity strengthens

initial_npcs.name: Elder Moss Thaurin
initial_npcs.description: Commune founder, now elderly. Built Storm Garden from nothing. Remembers when there were only twelve of them. Will not abandon what they've built, but won't sacrifice the community to stubbornness either.

initial_npcs.name: Defender Chief Bren Karsel
initial_npcs.description: Leads the commune's volunteer defenders. Forty fighters against three ships of professionals. Knows they can't win a straight fight. Looking for asymmetric options.

initial_npcs.name: Fugitive Technician Sera Vox
initial_npcs.description: Former House of Vox broadcast technician who fled with damaging information. The commune gave her sanctuary. Now Vox wants her back. She knows they'll make an example of her.

initial_npcs.name: The Storm Children
initial_npcs.description: Thirty-seven children born in Storm Garden, never registered in the Codex. If the commune falls, they'll be processed as 'anomalies' and separated. The stakes.

_design_notes: Four commune members trying to save their community from three different threats. The Negotiator plays factions against each other. The Defender prepares for the fight they hope won't come. The Smuggler knows the hidden routes. The Ritualist might have spiritual leverage. This isn't about winning fights - it's about community survival against corporations and factions that see them as resources or obstacles. 20 rounds of negotiation, misdirection, and the question of what you'll sacrifice to protect what you've built.

players.name: Negotiator Lira Thaurin
goals: Find a way to make Storm Garden too valuable or too costly to take
Play the three factions against each other if possible
Protect the commune without betraying its principles (hardest part)

players.name: Defender Kade Eluun
goals: Prepare defenses that make assault too costly
Train volunteers for the fight they hope won't come
Find the weak points in the enemy forces - everyone has weak points

players.name: Smuggler Yara Karsel
goals: Identify escape routes if they need to evacuate
Find something valuable enough to trade for safety
Maybe call in some favors from the Freeborn network - if they'll answer

players.name: Ritualist Dex Ossai
goals: Use the commune's collective ritual strength as leverage
Commune with the ley-station's dormant systems - maybe it still has power
Protect the children at any cost - they are the future

_beats: Crisis Council - the three ships, what each wants, commune resources
Initial Contact - negotiating with ACG, Vox, Tempest separately
Intelligence Gathering - what leverage do they have? What weaknesses?
Community Pressure - some want to fight, some want to flee, unity straining
First Ultimatum - one faction escalates, decision point
Playing Factions - can they be turned against each other?
The Hidden Card - the ley-station's dormant systems, Sera's dangerous information
Escalation - violence imminent or begun, last-ditch options
The Deal - what must be sacrificed to survive? Who decides?
Resolution - commune intact, scattered, or something new

_mission_objectives.description: Ensure Storm Garden commune survives the three-faction threat
Protect the fugitive and the children from extraction
Find leverage or allies that change the power balance

notes: RESONANCE COMMUNE SURVIVAL - Community under siege. Three factions want something, the commune has forty fighters and two hundred people to protect. This isn't about heroics - it's about survival, negotiation, and what you'll sacrifice to protect what you've built together. 20 rounds of crisis management, faction play, and the question of what community means when the system wants you gone.
